# Buddies task review and proposed execution plan — September 15, 2026

Owner direction: “Let's plan it out in tasks before we do work and review all the tasks.” This dated record reviews 68 existing native records: 66 Lead-owned projects and the two known supervised repair projects. Full criteria and todos were read for all 31 unfinished records; 37 closed records received an inventory/history review, not a fresh completion re-audit. The new restart-integration child brings this reviewed set to 69 records and 32 unfinished outcomes/umbrellas. This is not a workspace-wide census of other teams.

Native Tasks own live status, ownership, criteria and next actions. The table below records the planning disposition at this date. No implementation, tests, staff dispatch or release is part of this planning turn. Proposed execution Tasks are held for owner review; this is the owner's requested sequencing, not a new permission rule.

## Scope and Worker terminology

The current core defines a Worker as an ordinary Buddy in temporary Worker mode, with exactly one parent manager relationship; it can receive several related Tasks. Its own identity/memory persists across those Tasks, and its conversations hold execution history. An ephemeral harness sub-agent is a different mechanism. The owner's question about temporary identity requests clarification; it does not by itself approve or reject a redesign. This plan retains the current model and adds clear terminology to affected owner-facing help/docs without introducing a new lifetime or controller. Staffing or automatic-retirement changes require a separate concrete workflow decision.

## Proposed work order

| 0 | Repair/reconciliation umbrella `buddy_project_37f2780f-f766-452b-991c-eb4ca4192a9b` | Compare all old open criteria with later evidence. Propose keep, complete, supersede, defer or externally blocked per criterion; preserve the original failed attempts. Do not mistake this planning inventory for completion of the underlying code/browser checks. |
| 1 | New restart candidate `buddy_project_62511186-9ab4-4ec6-aece-4bdf39307527` | Integrate only missing final restart corrections into a stable isolated candidate; prove same-audience resume, provider mismatch exclusion and inferred-session recovery. Hand exact candidate evidence to existing release work. |
| 2 | Summaries `buddy_project_075e367e-3442-474c-a58d-8094aec59e25` | Qualify loaded implementation, representative four-project summary ≤15,000 characters, full expansion, bounded fields, privacy and complete MCP-envelope measurement. |
| 3 | Assignment settings `buddy_project_4abf69fe-7981-4934-aaa0-7b4d2908906e` | Qualify current send/config implementation at actual invocation; requested/resolved/admitted settings agree, queued choices stay deterministic and continuation mismatch is explicit. |
| 3a | Incremental reads `buddy_project_56ced029-2ce3-4897-b037-462d5a01e2ff` | After summary contract, specify exact current filter/cursor semantics and test updates/access changes without silent gaps. Document whether restart-on-stale is sufficient; justify any true change-feed work separately. |
| 4 | Usage `buddy_project_cdae619b-6e1d-4d5b-9c78-84308f418344` | Report known usage/time once per constituent attempt, including retry/review lineage; unknown stays null with reasons. Avoid double counting and distinguish elapsed time from summed concurrent work. |
| 5 | Review wakeups `buddy_project_4f875aff-3481-4ba9-8aab-eb0ea62c1308` | Reproduce redundant attention, then group compatible nonurgent wakeups through existing scheduling with a maximum delay; retain each result and urgent route, stop fences and original limits. |
| 6 | Integrated UI/runtime acceptance `buddy_project_67c0de12-9b60-4748-ae8b-0a88792c2f74` | Inspect criteria, settings and usage through actual owner/tool flows; clear temporary Worker terminology; one bounded authorized loaded-path workflow and coherent source/build evidence. |
| Supporting | Existing UI repair `buddy_project_95592e35-f568-4868-9a93-03c8a8511597` | Qualify saved-grant revocation, dirty drafts and exact original-thread history in the browser; repair only a remaining reproduction. Preserve this owner instead of creating another UI task. |
| Delivery | Existing release `buddy_project_a2047be3-f8cb-4eed-ac2e-522e3831bee6` | Assemble accepted restart/efficiency/UI changes with attributable commits and appropriate checks. Record candidate, pushed and loaded versions separately. |

Efficiencies may ship as independent slices. The final integration Task verifies composition; it must not force every delivery to wait for telemetry or batching. Summary and selection work starts from the already-present implementation. The existing diagnostic project supplies setup/admission/return truth. UI/history acceptance remains separately attributable even where one browser session can cover several criteria. Suggested owners remain the Lead for API/runtime acceptance, the existing UI Engineer for UI repairs, and the existing Release Engineer for assembly; no new assignment or execution allowance has been sent.

## Review verdict

The plan has concrete outcomes and mostly suitable real-boundary checks. The main problems were stale starting assumptions and overlapping old execution instructions. Keep six efficiency child Tasks, clarify their starting evidence, add one missing restart-integration child, and reuse the existing reconciliation/UI/release work. Do not reopen completed Worker design, restore hiring quotas, add another scheduler, change the package format, or expand into external mailbox/scientific work to satisfy historical text.

Gaps to resolve during the planned slices: stable source/build identity after concurrent edits; original/representative consumer corpus qualification; actual assignment invocation matching; precise deletion/access-change cursor guarantees; available usage coverage and units; maximum review batching delay; the exact remaining UI/history evidence. The initial inbox test failure followed by success remains in the prior progress evidence; it is not a persistent defect established by this planning pass.

## Decision history and evidence

Decision-maker: owner for planning-before-work; assistant for decomposition/order and proposed dispositions. No owner approval of every detailed mechanism is implied. Successor to the earlier efficiency plan and progress review; earlier files remain unchanged.

Why retain the six children: payload size, cursor correctness, invocation configuration, usage attribution, attention scheduling and composition have distinct proof obligations. Why add one child: the final restart patch is verified locally but absent from the earlier main delivery, and needs a bounded integration handoff. Why keep old records: later fixes do not retroactively turn failed attempts into successful ones, and broad historical checklists contain both valid invariants and obsolete mechanisms.

Tradeoff: separate acceptance adds modest coordination overhead. Avoid duplicated implementation by inspecting the changed artifact once and linking its evidence to the relevant criteria. Revisit task separation if two slices share one coherent small patch, or if a stable current build proves a remaining task already complete. A question about Worker identity is not sufficient evidence to reverse the core design.

# Wave_sim efficiency task plan — September 15, 2026

Planning record by Buddies Development Lead. The owner requested: “if there is work here plan it out, write the tasks.” The scope is the newly created Wave_sim coordination-efficiency project, which had three broad todos. The detailed decomposition below is the assistant's planning choice; it does not record owner acceptance of every proposed runtime mechanism.

Parent Task: `buddy_project_6efaffd1-0415-4dcf-80a4-bb6599d924b7`.

## Outcome and sequence

Make it cheaper in context and time to discover changed work, assign the intended model, inspect actual effort, and review worker results.

| Task | Deliverable | Dependency |
|---|---|---|
| Compact summaries | Bounded work/inbox/team discovery, full expansion, measured four-project summary ≤15,000 serialized characters | First delivery |
| Incremental reads | Reliable recent/actionable reads and documented cursor/removal/access-change semantics | Summary contract |
| Assignment selection | Requested/resolved/admitted provider, model and effort through common conversation configuration | Next delivery after summaries |
| Usage reporting | Deduplicated assignment-tree usage and time with explicit coverage | Selection receipts and causal IDs |
| Review wakeups | Bounded coalescing through existing Mail/return scheduling, with each return retained | Return attribution and usage observations |
| UI and integration | Owner views, boundary regression, build provenance and representative workflow qualification | Prepare fixtures early; accept after all five slices |

Suggested delivery order: summaries → selection → usage → review wakeups. Incremental-read work follows the summary contract and is independently reviewable. Integration consumes all slices. Each implementation slice includes its own verification; the final task checks their composition.

## Native Tasks

### 1. Finish compact Buddy work and attention summaries

Task: `buddy_project_075e367e-3442-474c-a58d-8094aec59e25`

Let a lead discover current work without repeatedly loading full historical criteria and evidence. Reconcile and finish the summary code already being edited in shared/src/buddy-resources.ts; reuse existing work, inbox and team read authorities.

Acceptance: A frozen representative four-project fixture produces a summary of at most 15,000 serialized characters. Report the normalized payload and complete MCP envelope sizes separately, with measured read latency. Summary fields are bounded and include IDs, revisions, owner, status, update time, blocker/next-action previews, todo/evidence counts, truncation and expansion refs. Full criteria, history and comments remain accessible under the same audience. `server/src/buddies/assignment-config.ts` reuses the canonical configuration
resolver and required-MCP provider check. The dispatch path validates the exact
recipient/project/continuation route before looking up its configuration.
Unsupported selections fail before enqueueing or creating a return conversation.

The original config is part of the package command's idempotency payload. Its
first host resolution is stored as `policy.assignment_config` on recipient
attempts. No new database column is required. Same-key replay retains it; a
different config under the same key conflicts. Retries, managed continuations
and interruption reports retain the selection. Parent return policies explicitly
remove it so selecting a worker's model does not select the lead's model.

Fresh conversation creation takes a pinned `ConversationConfig`, preserving the
existing creation/replay/configuration boundary. Reused conversations must match
the requested effective provider/model/effort. Changed configuration between send
and invocation fails with `assignment_config_conflict`; no different provider
request is invoked and no actual execution snapshot is recorded.

The earlier execution receipt sampled conversation getters before preflight.
It now records the resolved configuration immediately before `executeTurn`.
The native integration test compares that receipt with the actual request passed
to the provider adapter. This proves host invocation configuration; it does not
prove a remote provider's internal model routing.

Moving `BuddyKnowledgeScopeSchema` into one small shared module removes the
circular dependency that otherwise results from reusing `ConversationConfig`
